subject: Aligning term architecture and staged uptake for Luminate Health renewal
messages:
From: Susan Park <susan@luminatehealth.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal window — aligning term & uptake for FY29

Mateo,

We're starting to line up our FY29 budget and want to discuss the renewal that comes up in Q4. Luminate is interested in a three-year commitment that gives us predictable unit pricing as we scale our inference workloads. Two constraints from procurement: (1) we'd like co-terming with an existing vendor window in Jan so our fiscal year lines up; (2) we need a phased ramp schedule (50% first 12 months, 30% second, 20% third) to accommodate pilot-to-production migration.

Can Redwood support a structured multi-year agreement with a formal ramp and an option to trigger extra capacity earlier if needed? Also — any objections to a soft auto-renew clause that requires 60-day notice to opt out?

Appreciate any high-level options and a ballpark on credits/price breaks for the commit. Would like a 30-min sync with you and procurement next week.

Best,
Susan Park
Head of Platform Engineering
Luminate Health

--
Attachment: Luminate_MAT_Questions.xlsx (spreadsheet with procurement checklist)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Susan Park <susan@luminatehealth.com>
Cc: camila.reyes@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal window — aligning term & uptake for FY29

Susan — thanks for the clear ask and the MAT. High-level: Redwood can absolutely support a three-year commit with a staged ramp and an earlier capacity trigger. We commonly do co-terming to a customer fiscal window and can put guardrails around auto-renew (60-day notice is fine).

Options I'd propose for your team to consider:
- Option A (Predictable): 3-year commit, anchored annual volumes with unit price step-downs at year boundaries. Built-in 25% burst capacity across the term. 60-day soft auto-renew.
- Option B (Staged Upside): 3-year commit with front-loaded onboarding credits (to ease pilot costs) and the 50/30/20 ramp you suggested encoded in the MOP. Overages billed at a pre-agreed blended rate.
- Option C (Flexible Co-term): 3-year nominal commit that co-terms to Jan fiscal window with quarterly true-ups and a defined early-trigger clause that converts reserved capacity to live capacity within 7 days.

I'll put together a concise proposal and a suggested MOP (milestones: pilot completion, production cutover, 12/24-mo checkpoints). Can Camila and Kimberly weigh in on pricing levers and whether we should recommend a convertible burst bucket vs. fixed burst?

Also proposing a 30-min call next Tue 6/19 at 10am PT — does that work on your end?

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: proposed_schedule.csv (high-level ramp table)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: camila.reyes@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Luminate renewal — pricing / contract structure input needed

Camila / Kimberly —

Quick thread: Luminate (Susan Park) wants a 3yr commit, co-termed to Jan, staged ramp 50/30/20 and a soft auto-renew (60d). I attached their MAT and the high-level schedule I sent.

Questions:
1) Pricing: can we offer a 12% unit discount on year-1 committed volumes, stepping to 16% in year-2 and 20% in year-3 (blended effective across consumed tokens)? Or do we prefer a flat blended discount if they want more flexibility?
2) Burst model: recommend a convertible burst bucket (they can convert to reserved with 7-day notice) or a fixed burst % with pre-agreed rates?
3) Legal: do we add a hard true-up cadence (quarterly) or annual true-up? Procurement prefers quarterly true-ups but that increases SOW complexity.

I've penciled a call Tue 6/19 10am PT with Susan + procurement. Can you both review and I can bring a draft commercial slide to the call.

Thanks —
Mateo

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Luminate renewal — pricing / contract structure input needed

Thanks — quick thoughts inline: 

1) Pricing: the stepped discount you propose is reasonable and aligns with typical consumption curves. To make it procurement-friendly, offer both (a) stepped discount schedule with committed volumes by year, and (b) a blended effective rate option they can choose at signing. The stepped approach gives us upsell runway.

2) Burst model: recommend convertible burst bucket. Operationally it's easier for Luminate to start with a burst buffer they can convert; it reduces the procurement ask to "option to convert" rather than an upfront larger reserved bucket. We'll define conversion terms (7 days) and a conversion floor (50% of burst).

3) True-up cadence: quarterly true-ups preferred for visibility but add a small annual reconciliation to simplify invoicing. For the contract, include an option to switch to annual true-ups after the first 12 months if both parties agree.

Commercial ask: offer an onboarding credit equivalent to 10% of year-1 committed spend to smooth pilot costs (redeemable against months 1–6).

I'll draft a short commercial slide and a redline snippet for the MOP. Kim — can you confirm whether finance is comfortable with 10% onboarding credit and the proposed stepped discounts?

- Camila

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Susan Park <susan@luminatehealth.com>, Luminate Health Procurement <procurement@luminatehealth.com>
Cc: camila.reyes@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 2 Jul 2028 15:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposal: 3-year anchored commit + staged uptake (proposal attached)

Susan — thanks again for the sync. Attached is a concise proposal (Redwood_Proposal_Luminate_3yr_v1.pdf) that captures the commercial and operational structure we discussed:

- Term: 36 months, co-term to Jan fiscal window (co-term effective date: 2029-01-01)
- Ramp schedule: Year 1 = 50% committed baseline, Year 2 = 30%, Year 3 = 20% (volumes expressed as % of total committed units).
- Pricing: stepped discounts — 12% (Y1), 16% (Y2), 20% (Y3) off list per-unit rates, with a blended elective at signing if preferred.
- Burst: convertible burst bucket equal to 30% of Year-1 committed volume; conversion to reserved possible with 7-day notice (conversion floor: 50% of burst).
- Onboarding credit: 10% of Year-1 committed spend, redeemable across first 6 billing periods.
- True-ups: quarterly operational true-ups + annual reconciliation; option to move to annual after Year 1 by mutual agreement.
- Auto-renew: 60-day soft auto-renew with an executive-level review trigger prior to renewal date.

Next steps I propose:
1) Procurement review and confirm: (a) co-term date, (b) acceptance of convertible burst mechanics, (c) DocuSign-ready commercial terms.
2) If accepted, we'll prepare a short SOW + MOP with milestones (pilot complete, production cutover) and a mutual action plan.

I attached the proposal PDF and included a DocuSign link to the initial commercial sheet for fast review. If this structure looks right we can convert to legal redlines and have a countersign target of 2028-08-01 to meet their procurement windows.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Regards,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
